name: Zeni Geva
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: A Tokyo trio named for money and violence flew to Chicago in 1991 to be recorded by Steve Albini, and kept going back for the next decade.

eras.title: Money, violence, and a cassette
eras.text: KK Null had already done time in the Tokyo noise scene with YBO2 when he started a band with a vocalist, a second guitarist and a drummer from Hanatarash. The name was a joke about money and German violence. The music was not.

years.src: Wikipedia: KK Null · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva · Trouser Press: Zeni Geva · Bandcamp Daily: Zeni Geva and Beyond
years.h: [[KK Null|9c51604c-a456-4e3e-8f85-cc96ec0df439]] starts Zeni Geva as a quartet in Tokyo
years.p: Null, guitarist Fumiyoshi Suzuki, vocalist Elle and drummer Ikuo Taketani debut with the record How to Kill. The name joins the Japanese word for money to the German word for violence.
years.xp:
Kazuyuki Kishino, born in Tokyo in 1961 and known as KK Null, had joined the noise and progressive rock group YBO2 in 1984 and trained in Butoh dance. He put out How to Kill in 1987 on his own NUX Organization label.

Monumental Movement reads the name as "Zeni" (money) plus "Gewalt" (violence). Trouser Press and the Bandcamp Daily primer both list Taketani, whose résumé also includes Hanatarash and the Boredoms, in the early lineup.

years.h: Mitsuru Tabata joins on guitar and stays for 24 years
years.p: Bassist Bunsho Nishikawa replaces Elle, the cassette Vast Impotenz appears, and [[Tatsuya Yoshida|7a82840d-beb5-4819-aed3-6b732332b461]] of [[Ruins|8ca7f2ea-6a8d-412d-a188-f75abea72b67]] briefly takes the drum stool.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates Tabata's arrival to 1988 and his exit to 2012. Yoshida played for a spell in 1988 and again around 1990 before leaving to concentrate on Ruins.

eras.title: Down to three, up to sixteen minutes
eras.text: The lineup settled into a trio with no bass, and the songs got longer. It was the sound the West would hear first.

years.src: Scaruffi: Zeni Geva · Wikipedia: Zeni Geva
years.h: Maximum Money Monster opens with a 16-minute track
years.p: Scaruffi counts it as the record where the band stopped sounding like a hardcore group. It came out on Null's NUX Organization label.
years.xp: The album was reissued in 2007. A live clip from 1990 with Yoshida on drums is on YouTube.

eras.title: A flight to Chicago
eras.text: Zeni Geva crossed the Pacific to record with Steve Albini, then Albini crossed back. The two trips produced the records that made the band's name in the West.

years.cap: Total Castration, cover art by Stephen Holman
years.src: Ghost Cult Magazine: Zeni Geva · IDIOTEQ: From Tokyo flyers · Wikipedia: Zeni Geva
years.h: Total Castration, recorded at Albini's house in Chicago
years.p: David Hopkins of Public Bath Records invited Zeni Geva over. They tracked the album with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] at his home studio, The Basement.
years.xp:
Tabata says the band flew to Chicago in the autumn of 1991 at the invitation of Hopkins, who then ran Public Bath. Eito Noro was now on drums, replacing Yoshida.

The album is the first of five Zeni Geva records Albini worked on. Skin Graft announced a first-ever vinyl pressing, on gold vinyl, for October 30, 2026. Null said no one would be happier to see it than Hopkins, who died in 2022.

years.h: Neurosis share a bill with Zeni Geva at San Francisco's Kennel Club
years.p: Mason Jones of Charnel Music had introduced Neurosis to the band. After the show, Neurosis's Steve Von Till says they were sold.
years.xp: Neurot's Deep Cut post credits Jones with the introduction and the 1992 Kennel Club gig with convincing the label. Von Till: "After seeing them live and listening to their early records, we were completely blown away." Neurot released 10,000 Light Years nine years later.

years.h: Tabata hands out flyers for Albini's Japan tour outside Nakano Sunplaza
years.p: Nirvana fans were leaving the hall talking about "Smells Like Teen Spirit". Albini landed the next month.
years.xp: IDIOTEQ's account of the tour: Albini played Shinjuku Antinoch on March 20, Koenji 20000VOLT on March 31 and Osaka's Juso Fandango on April 3, with sessions squeezed in at Afterbeat studio in Koenji.

years.src: Lambgoat: Zeni Geva · IDIOTEQ: From Tokyo flyers
years.h: Albini plays guitar with Zeni Geva at Koenji 20000VOLT
years.p: A cover of Godflesh, recorded to 16 tracks in front of the crowd, ends up on the 2026 box Superunit: Maximum Implosion.
years.xp:
The band released the Albini material under two names: "Zeni Geva & Steve Albini" for existing songs and "Superunit" for new ones with bassist MAS-P of Captain Condom. Albini brought his own microphones, a Veleno aluminum guitar, and a pool cue in a case with a Jesus Lizard sticker on it.

Big Black and Rapeman songs were kept out of the set. The other covers let Albini take vocals, including Kraftwerk's "The Model".

years.h: Albini finds the dbx switch at Afterbeat
years.p: IDIOTEQ says he crouched under the console flipping switches until the studio's dbx noise reduction was off. He objected to what it did to dynamic range.
years.xp: On the song "Shirushi" he pushed Null's vocals into distortion using tricks from home cassette recording. Told that digital effects could do more, he insisted tape speed manipulation was the better route.

eras.title: Biafra's label, Albini's basement
eras.text: Jello Biafra's Alternative Tentacles signed the band and put out two albums and a single. Albini produced the records and the West began to notice.

years.h: The Disgraceland 7-inch is Alternative Tentacles catalog number 127
years.p: It is the band's first release on Jello Biafra's label.

years.src: Alternative Tentacles: Desire For Agony · Wikipedia: Desire for Agony · Wikipedia: Alternative Tentacles discography
yt: Stigma and Dead Sun Rising, live
years.h: Desire for Agony · Virus 135, recorded at Albini's basement
years.p: Alternative Tentacles calls it the band's full-length debut for the label and one of the most extreme records in noise-core. Wikipedia lists a September 1993 session at The Basement in Chicago.
years.xp:
The album runs 38 minutes and 28 seconds. The cover painting is by Mark Fischer. Discogs dates the CD to 1994, while Wikipedia and the Alternative Tentacles discography say 1993.

AllMusic's Patrick Kennedy compared it to Motörhead meets King Crimson.

years.src: Wikipedia: Freedom Bondage · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva
years.h: Freedom Bondage is recorded in France, with Albini again
years.p: Zeni Geva track it in June at Black Box studio. Noro is still on drums.
years.xp: The album is nine tracks and 38 minutes 32 seconds, ending with the 10:58 "Ground Zero". The Austin Chronicle reviewed it that November. Monumental Movement calls it the record where acoustic texture, structure and violence balance best.

eras.title: New drummer, new machine
eras.text: Noro left, and the songs stretched past ten minutes. Null started building his own electronics, and the band signed to Neurosis's label.

years.src: Wikipedia: Zeni Geva · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva
years.h: Eito Noro leaves; Masataka Fujikake takes over drums
years.p: Blake Fleming sits in briefly first. Monumental Movement credits Fujikake with adding polyrhythmic density.
years.xp: Fleming is listed by Wikipedia as a temporary drummer in 1996. A Zeni Geva show in Braunschweig that year is on YouTube.

years.src: Neurot Recordings: Deep Cut · Scaruffi: Zeni Geva
years.h: 10,000 Light Years: Neurot, Electrical Audio, and the nulltron
years.p: Albini records it at his Chicago studio. Null adds a homemade device, the nulltron, that layers static and distortion over the guitars.
years.xp: Neurot calls it the band's seventh album. Scaruffi thinks it sounds almost like a parody of Zeni Geva, which shows the range of opinion on the record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Zeni Geva · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva
years.h: Zeni Geva goes quiet after a live album from Geneva
years.p: Last Nanosecond: Live in Geneva 2002 comes out in 2004. Null keeps releasing solo and collaborative work; Tabata works with Acid Mothers Temple.

eras.title: Ruins, again
eras.text: Yoshida came back on drums and the band toured again. The Albini recordings, and one of the labels that released them, kept surfacing.

years.src: Wikipedia: Zeni Geva · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva
years.h: Tatsuya Yoshida returns and the band tours again
years.p: A Tokyo show from March 2009 is on YouTube. The live album Alive and Rising, recorded that September, follows in 2010.

years.h: Tabata leaves after more than 20 years
years.p: Null and Yoshida tour Europe as a two-piece. Total Castration is remastered and reissued the same year.

years.src: IDIOTEQ: From Tokyo flyers · Lambgoat: Zeni Geva
years.h: Superunit: Maximum Implosion collects the Albini sessions
years.p: Skin Graft puts the 1992 Tokyo recordings on a Record Store Day double LP: the Nai-Ha album, studio tracks, and the live All Right, You Little Bastards!.
years.xp: Albini died on May 7, 2024, at Electrical Audio in Chicago, according to IDIOTEQ. The set includes Tabata's memoir The Future Belongs to Analog Loyalists. A riff from "Painwise" turned up later in Shellac's "The Guy Who Invented Fire".
